oncall-bot: ALERT triggered 2013456789 - log-rule: repeated 503s from runtime-adapter in us-west-2 (auto-pager)
Maya (oncall): acked — I'm on it, pinging infra + obs. Any customer reports yet? @PD Bot link? :eyes:
PD Bot: Incident page created: https://redwood.incidents/INC-201345 - priority: P2 - triggered by log-rule:runtime-adapter-5xx
Ethan: digging in metrics — saw a sharp spike at 01:11 UTC, ~2k 503s/min for ~5m, source host group runtime-adapter-prod-{a,b}. CPU fine, connections look normal. Traces show request hangs going into the backend pool.
Priya: from error logs — a flood of "timeout reading upstream" and a recurring pattern where the adapter logs include a malformed JSON header for some requests. Sample:
```
[2026-03-15T01:11:22Z] runtime-adapter error: upstream read timeout, request="{\"id\":\"abc123\",\"meta\":\"\x1b\"}"
```
Ethan: that \x1b escape looks like a non-printable char from a downstream probe/service. Likely a bad health-check or probe hitting production path.
Maya (oncall): ok immediate plan: 1) silence the noisy pager for this rule for 30m while we triage 2) add a quick log-filter to exclude known probe pattern from pager 3) notify SRE rotation to follow up and make a permanent signature.
SRE Rotation: I'll take the follow-up. Going to push a temporary suppression and add a regex exclusion on the live rule. Proposed query tweak (kql):
```
source:runtime-adapter AND status:503 AND NOT message:/\\x1b|probe-check|health-probe/i
```
Maya (oncall): execute suppression now: `./tools/pagerctl silence --rule runtime-adapter-5xx --dur 30m --reason "known probe flood, triage in progress"` :white_check_mark:
LogWatcher: suppression applied by Maya. Alert volume down ~95% in last 2m.
Priya: created MR with permanent signature and test: https://github.com/redwood/infra-alerts/pull/432 - adds new signature `probe-escaped-meta` that excludes probe payloads but keeps other 5xxs. MR includes unit-test log samples and CI job.
Ethan: quick mitigation notes — also raised threshold for the alert from 50/min to 200/min for the next 12 hours to reduce noise while we verify. Config change: `alert.threshold.rate = 200` in repo path `infra/alerts/runtime-adapter.yml`.
Maya (oncall): documenting customer impact: observed increased 5xxs for ~5-8 minutes, retry backoff handled most requests, no large-scale data loss. A handful of dedicated customers in us-west-2 reported increased latency (support ticket ids: #8241, #8242). Marking impact as degraded but limited.
SRE Rotation: after triage we found a misconfigured canary probe in staging that started hitting prod hostnames after a deploy diff. Posting remediation steps in the MR — rolling back that probe and adding strict host whitelisting for probes.
Priya: tests in MR include these log lines; added a note for oncall runbook to prefer signature-match over broad regex filters. Also created a dashboard panel in Obs called "runtime-adapter 5xx by signature" and a pinned query to quickly flip between all 5xx vs excluded-probes.
Maya (oncall): follow-ups tracked in the MR and incident doc: 1) merge signature MR 2) add CI guard to prevent probe config from pointing at prod 3) revert temporary threshold after 24h 4) postmortem in weekly incident review.
Ethan: small note — please don't suppress full-body logs; the signature intentionally matches the escaped-meta pattern. See MR description for examples.
SRE Rotation: merging MR now, will monitor for regressions. If anything slips through we will revert suppression and open a live page.
Maya (oncall): handing off to SRE Rotation for the next 8h. Paging suppression will auto-expire at 2013458589 — I'll extend if we still see noise. Thanks all :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Handoff recorded — oncall: SRE Rotation. Pager silence expires at 2013458589.
LogWatcher: last check — error rate back to baseline ~3/min. No active customer-facing incidents. Will keep dashboard alerts at medium sensitivity.
Maya (oncall): closing the thread here, file the postmortem link when ready. Good job everyone.
SRE Rotation: adding final note to incident doc: root cause = misdirected probe payload causing parser edge-case; fixes: signature, probe whitelisting, alert threshold tuning, dashboard. :heavy_check_mark:
